rounds.text: The bull case points to a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 106 per share [E34] and a 3-year compounded sales growth of 25% [E14]. Conceded: [E34]. However, the fundamental financial reality shows severe stress beneath the surface, highlighted by a negative cash conversion of -1.45x and negative operating cash flow of Rs -7.32 Cr in Mar 2026 [E24, E25]. Free cash flow is similarly distressed at Rs -9.46 Cr [E26], while borrowings have jumped sharply to Rs 33.67 Cr [E29]. Working capital has deteriorated significantly as debtor days increased from 88.6 to 111 days and overall working capital days rose from 24.4 to 64.7 days [E43, E44]. Furthermore, reported earnings are inflated by Rs 4.02 Cr of other income [E42], and filings flag potential interest capitalization [E41]. Compounding these operational warning signs, promoters have aggressively exited, slashing their holding by 21.87 percentage points from 78.30% down to 56.43% [E31].

The bear’s focus on negative cash flow [E25, E26] ignores the company’s active transition into a capital-intensive growth phase, evidenced by a 1409.1% surge in capital work-in-progress [E30]. While the bear highlights rising debt [E29], this leverage remains at a moderate 0.64x [E27], supporting the necessary infrastructure expansion that has already driven a 204% compounded profit growth over three years [E16]. Conceded: the increase in debtor and working capital days [E43, E44] and the negative cash conversion [E24]. However, the bear’s alarm regarding promoter selling [E31] overlooks the simultaneous entry of domestic institutional investors, who have increased their stake from 0.00% to 1.15% [E32], signaling growing professional confidence. Furthermore, the bear’s critique of "other income" [E42] fails to acknowledge that the company has successfully expanded its operating margin by 2 percentage points over the last three years [E21]. Ultimately, the market is currently pricing the stock at a 21.4% discount to its intrinsic value [E35], suggesting that the current operational headwinds are already more than accounted for in the share price.
